steps.name: Sample structure QC
steps.question: Do the 6 aldosterone-treated and 6 vehicle-control kidney samples separate by condition on a blind variance-stabilized PCA, and are there outlier samples or unexpected structure before testing?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC (blind vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap) per R-0033, template tpl-qc-eda@1.0.0

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv, build a DESeqDataSet, apply vst(blind=TRUE), compute PCA on the top 500 most variable genes, plot a sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap, and report library sizes per sample colored by condition (treated/control).
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample distance heatmap produced for all 12 samples
Library size per sample reported and compared to the 6 vs 6 group median
Any sample that fails to cluster with its condition group is flagged explicitly

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: aldosterone-treated vs control
caveats: Counts are gene-level from Salmon but only the summarized count matrix was supplied (no per-sample quant.sf transcript files), so no tximport length-offset correction can be applied; state this limitation rather than approximating it.
At n=6/group DESeq2 flags rather than replaces count outliers (below the 7-replicate switch point) — report the count of NA-padj genes from this cause separately from independent-filtering NAs.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 6 aldosterone-treated and 6 vehicle-control kidney samples?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test + apeglm shrinkage as primary method with edgeR QLF as the robustness second method per R-0001/R-0042, template tpl-deseq2-two-group@1.0.0

steps.description: Filter to genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (the smallest group size). Build DESeqDataSet from counts.csv and metadata.csv with condition as an explicit factor, reference level set to 'control' (or vehicle, whichever the metadata names as untreated), contrast named condition: treated vs control. Run DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization and the Wald test. Apply apeglm log2 fold-change shrinkage on the treated-vs-control coefficient. Report both the unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering at alpha=0.05, and flag genes with an NA p-value from Cook's-distance count-outlier flagging (expected given n=6 per group, below the 7-replicate threshold at which DESeq2 switches to replacement). Separately run an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design as a robustness check; report the number of significant genes (padj<0.05) from each method and the size/identity of the intersection as the high-confidence gene set, plus genes unique to one method. Produce MA plot and dispersion plot diagnostics. Save the full DESeq2 results table (ranked by shrunken log2FC for the table/plots) with the Wald 'stat' column retained for downstream ranked enrichment/TF-activity use.
acceptance_criteria: Full DESeq2 results table with baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for every tested gene
Number of genes tested after pre-filter and number significant at padj<0.05 reported
edgeR QLF results computed on identical filtered counts/design; overlap and per-method-unique gene counts reported
MA plot and dispersion plot produced
Reference level and contrast direction (treated vs control) stated explicitly

steps.name: Preranked GSEA: Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways
caveats: If fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05, do not run an over-representation test on that short list — the ranked GSEA on the full list is the primary and sufficient method here.
Enrichment results are method-dependent; present sets as hypotheses, not proven findings.
steps.question: Which biological pathways and processes are coordinately altered between aldosterone-treated and control kidney samples, using the full ranked gene list rather than an arbitrary significance cutoff?

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic, Hallmark first then Reactome/WikiPathways follow-up per R-0098/R-0165, all three collections confirmed present in the reference store

steps.description: Map gene symbols in the DESeq2 results table to the identifier space of each gene set collection, reporting the unmapped share. Rank all tested genes (post pre-filter) by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat' column). Run fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets) as the primary collection, then separately against Reactome pathways and WikiPathways human pathways as follow-up collections (each from the reference store, releases stated: MSigDB 2026.1, Reactome current, WikiPathways 2026.07.10). Apply a gene set size window of 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. Adjust p-values with BH within each collection; do not merge collections. Collapse redundant significant sets and report leading-edge genes for each significant set.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run separately on Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways with each collection's release stated
Ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald stat) stated explicitly
Gene sets restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with tested genes
Leading-edge genes reported for every significant set (padj<0.05) in each collection
Share of gene symbols that failed to map to each collection's identifier space reported

steps.name: Transcription factor activity inference (CollecTRI / decoupleR)
caveats: CollecTRI/DoRothEA are generic prior-knowledge networks, not kidney-specific regulons; a TF acting only in kidney tissue could be missed and a silent target in kidney adds noise — state this explicitly.

With n=6/group and no ARACNe/VIPER context-specific network available or supportable at this sample size (would need ~100+ samples), activity inference is limited to the prior-knowledge-network approach; do not present it as a context-specific regulon result.
steps.question: Which transcription factors show inferred activity changes between aldosterone-treated and control kidney samples, based on the coordinated behavior of their target genes?

grounding.reason: TF activity via decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI (primary) with DoRothEA confidence A-C (secondary) per R-0111/R-0113, both regulon files confirmed present in the reference store

steps.description: Using the DESeq2 Wald statistic of every tested gene (not only the significant ones) from T1S2, run decoupleR's univariate linear model (ulm) method against the CollecTRI human transcription-factor regulon network from the reference store, keeping the signed mode-of-regulation (activating/repressing) of each edge. Test a regulator only when at least 5 of its target genes are among the tested genes; report the number of regulators that entered the test. Rank transcription factors by inferred activity score (normalized enrichment/z-score) and report the top up- and down-activity TFs with their target overlap and score, alongside DoRothEA (confidence A-C, from the reference store) as a secondary cross-check for the top hits.
acceptance_criteria: decoupleR ulm run on the CollecTRI human regulon network (present in reference store) using the full Wald-statistic-ranked gene list
Number of regulators tested (>=5 targets among tested genes) reported
Ranked table of TF activity scores produced with direction of activity and number of contributing targets per TF
DoRothEA confidence A-C regulons used as a secondary cross-check for the top-ranked TFs, with agreement/disagreement stated

steps.name: Integrated report: DE genes, pathways, and TF activity
steps.question: What is the integrated, reproducible summary of which genes change with aldosterone treatment in kidney and which transcription factors are inferred to drive those changes?

grounding.reason: no single rule covers the report-assembly step as a whole; individual reporting requirements are grounded per the listed claims

steps.description: Assemble a single report combining: the DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap gene table (high-confidence DE set) with shrunken/unshrunken log2FC, lfcSE, and padj; the MA and dispersion diagnostic plots; the p-value histogram from the DE test; the fgsea Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways results with leading-edge genes; and the decoupleR CollecTRI TF activity ranking with the DoRothEA cross-check. State design (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch), thresholds (padj<0.05, BH, independent filtering), package versions (DESeq2, edgeR, apeglm, fgsea, decoupler), gene set collection releases, regulon network version, random seeds used for any resampling/permutation step, and number of genes tested/significant. State the tximport/length-offset limitation and the generic (non-kidney-specific) regulon limitation explicitly as caveats rather than omitting them.
acceptance_criteria: Report includes DE gene table, fit diagnostics, p-value histogram, enrichment results with leading edges, and TF activity ranking in one document
All package versions, thresholds, gene set/regulon collection releases, and seeds are stated
Both stated caveats (no length-offset correction; generic regulon network) appear explicitly
Number of tested and significant genes per method (DESeq2, edgeR) and their overlap size are stated

plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle control, unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level Salmon counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples). The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 pipeline: QC of sample structure, minimal low-count pre-filter, DESeq2 Wald test with median-of-ratios normalization and apeglm shrinkage as the primary DE test, edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as a robustness cross-check (per R-0001/R-0042, both are appropriate at n=6/group and their overlap is the high-confidence gene set), BH-adjusted significance calling with independent filtering, fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) then Reactome and WikiPathways (follow-up, all present in the reference store) on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, and decoupleR ulm transcription factor activity inference on the CollecTRI human regulon network (present in the reference store) using the same Wald statistic across all tested genes — directly answering 'which TFs sit behind the changes'. A final report step integrates the DE table, fit diagnostics, enrichment, and TF activity into one reproducible summary with package versions and thresholds stated. No count-matrix-only offset/length correction is applied since only gene-level counts (not tximport quant.sf transcript files) were provided — this is stated as a caveat rather than silently assumed away.

steps.method: Minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
DESeqDataSetFromMatrix on gene-level counts.csv, explicit reference level = control, contrast = condition treated vs control
DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage; edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as second method for robustness overlap
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI human regulons using the Wald statistic of all tested genes
Integrated DE + enrichment + TF activity report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
